mainTopic: The פסוקים about a טמא person and holy food, the touching rule for תרומה, and the laws of a פצוע דכא
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion of the פסוקים about a טמא person eating holy food. The גמרא shows that three separate פסוקים about תרומה are all needed. 'עד אשר יטהר' requires טבילה, 'ובא השמש' requires sunset, and 'עד מלאת' teaches that one need not wait for a קרבן כפרה. It then explains why both the יולדת and the זב need a פסוק about waiting for atonement before eating קדשים. Next, רבי זירא and a ברייתא teach that after טבילה but before nightfall, a person or vessel is already pure for מעשר but still makes תרומה impure by touching. A second source for this touching rule comes from 'בכל קדש לא תגע', read through a הקש to the מקדש. The גמרא then turns to the משנה about a פצוע דכא. רבי אלעזר and רבי יוחנן argue over whether his wife may eat תרומה because she 'already ate' before his injury. Finally, a ברייתא defines who counts as a פצוע דכא, and a man with one testicle is ruled כשר, like a סריס חמה. The amud ends as the גמרא begins challenging the punctured case with a story that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A verse that seems to be about תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the earlier reasoning by citing the פסוק 'בכל קדש לא תגע', which is read as including תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it written: 'She shall touch no holy thing' — which comes to include תרומה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a challenge. It points to a פסוק about the יולדת (a woman after childbirth) that is read as including תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier discussion did not count this פסוק as a source about תרומה. The challenge is that this פסוק is in fact expounded to include תרומה. That seems to clash with how the earlier verses were divided up.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written — a standard way to challenge using a פסוק
Holy thing; here read as including תרומה
To include — a word or phrase in the פסוק adds another case
The portion of produce given to a כהן, which must be eaten in purity

phrases.english: But isn't it written: 'She shall touch no holy thing'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 12:4, said about a woman after childbirth.

phrases.english: — to include תרומה!
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording; it doesn't change the meaning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning from the previous section of the daf.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier assumption about which פסוקים refer to תרומה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק that the earlier reasoning did not treat as a תרומה source is in fact expounded to include תרומה.

steps.title: The Torah lists separate matters one by one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the Torah counts several distinct matters separately. Not every phrase is about the same thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the verse counts each matter separately.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge. The Torah lists several different items, each with its own teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that all the phrases must point to one single subject. The answer is that the Torah teaches matter after matter, one at a time. So one פסוק including תרומה does not break the earlier reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather — introduces a new or corrected understanding
Matter by matter, separate items
It counts, it lists

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, קְרָא מִילֵּי מִילֵּי קָא חָשֵׁיב.
phrases.english: Rather, the verse counts separate matters one by one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, קְרָא מִילֵּי מִילֵּי קָא חָשֵׁיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting how the verses are structured
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All the phrases must refer to one subject, so including תרומה is a contradiction.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah lists distinct matters separately, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: Why three verses about תרומה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the Torah needs three different פסוקים teaching about a טמא person and תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why do I need three verses about תרומה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now has three פסוקים that all speak about eating תרומה after being טמא. It asks why so many are needed, which sets up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah does not repeat itself for nothing. If three פסוקים teach about the same topic, each must add something new. The גמרא will now show what each one adds.

keyTerms.meaning: Three verses
Why do I need it? — asks why a source seems extra

phrases.english: And why do I need three verses about תרומה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the conclusion that these פסוקים do teach about תרומה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What unique teaching each of the three פסוקים about תרומה provides.

steps.title: First verse needs the second: sunset is also required
steps.stepSummary: From 'עד אשר יטהר' alone we would not know how purity is reached. 'ובא השמש וטהר' teaches that sunset is also needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are needed. If we had only 'until he becomes pure', I would not know by what means. So the Torah wrote: 'and when the sun sets he is pure.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts explaining why each פסוק is needed. It begins with 'עד אשר יטהר' and shows what it leaves unclear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Until he becomes pure' tells us he must become pure, but not how. It could mean טבילה alone. 'ובא השמש וטהר' adds that he must also wait for הערב שמש (sunset) before eating תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: They are all needed
The Merciful One — a way of saying 'the Torah'
By what means?
And the sun sets — the requirement of הערב שמש

phrases.english: They are needed, for if from 'until he becomes pure'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:4

phrases.english: I would not know by what means he becomes pure
so the Merciful One wrote: 'And when the sun sets he is pure.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:7

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'ובא השמש וטהר' is needed to teach that sunset is required, not only purification in general.

steps.title: Second verse needs the third: no waiting for the קרבן כפרה
steps.stepSummary: From 'ובא השמש' alone, someone who must bring a קרבן כפרה might have to wait for it. 'עד מלאת' teaches that the completed days are enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the Torah wrote only 'and the sun sets', that would apply only to someone who does not need an atonement offering. But someone who needs an atonement offering, I might say must wait until he brings it. So the Torah wrote: 'until the days are complete.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues and shows what 'ובא השמש' alone would leave unclear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some טמאים, like a יולדת, must later bring a קרבן כפרה. We might think they cannot eat תרומה until that offering is brought. 'עד מלאת' about the יולדת teaches she may eat once her days are complete, even before bringing the קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: These words apply — this rule is limited to
Someone who needs an atonement offering
I might say
Until the days are complete

phrases.english: And if the Merciful One had written only 'and the sun sets'
that would apply only to one who does not need atonement
but for one who needs atonement
I might say: not until he brings his atonement
phrases.notes: Not eating תרומה until he brings his atonement offering.

phrases.english: so the Merciful One wrote: 'until the days are complete.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 12:4

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the answer, explaining why the third פסוק is needed.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'עד מלאת' teaches that one who owes a קרבן כפרה may eat תרומה once the days are complete, without waiting for the offering.

steps.title: Third verse needs the first: טבילה is still required
steps.stepSummary: From 'עד מלאת' alone we might think no טבילה is needed. 'עד אשר יטהר' teaches that immersion is still required.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the Torah wrote only 'until the days are complete', I would have said even without immersion. So the Torah wrote: 'until he becomes pure.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the circle. It shows why the first פסוק, 'עד אשר יטהר', is still needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'עד מלאת' sounds like the days finishing makes her pure on their own. 'עד אשר יטהר' shows that an act of purification, טבילה, is still needed. Now each of the three פסוקים has a unique job, which fully answers the question.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought (the mistaken first assumption)
Immersion in a מקוה
He becomes pure

steps.whatToRemember: Each פסוק teaches something unique: 'עד אשר יטהר' requires טבילה, 'ובא השמש' requires sunset, and 'עד מלאת' teaches that one does not wait for the קרבן כפרה.

phrases.english: And if the Merciful One had written only 'until the days are complete'
I would have said: even without immersion
so the Merciful One wrote: 'until he becomes pure.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer, showing the first פסוק is also needed.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'עד אשר יטהר' teaches that טבילה is required even after the days are complete.
steps.whyThisMatters: Together the three פסוקים give the full practical rule: a טמא person needs טבילה and sunset before eating תרומה, but does not need to wait for a קרבן כפרה.

steps.title: Why two verses about waiting for atonement before eating holy food?
steps.stepSummary: According to the תנא who argues with the school of רבי ישמעאל, 'עד אשר יטהר' means 'until he brings his atonement קרבן.' If so, why does the Torah need two פסוקים teaching that for קדשים?
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a תנא who disagrees with the school of רבי ישמעאל. He says the פסוק is talking about a זב who had three sightings and about a confirmed מצורע. For him, 'until he becomes pure' means 'until he brings his atonement offering.' If so, why do we need two פסוקים about holy food?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same kind of question again: why does the Torah repeat itself? This time it asks according to a different תנא's reading of 'עד אשר יטהר'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For this תנא, 'עד אשר יטהר' teaches that a זב or מצורע may not eat קדשים until he brings his קרבן. But the Torah already says the same about a יולדת ('וכפר עליה הכהן וטהרה'). So the גמרא asks why both פסוקים are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who had three discharges, so he must bring a קרבן to become fully pure
A confirmed מצורע, declared fully impure by the כהן
Atonement, meaning the atonement קרבן he must bring
Holy food from קרבנות

phrases.english: And according to that tanna who disagrees
with the tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael,
who says: about a zav who had three sightings
and about a confirmed metzora the verse is speaking,
phrases.notes: The פסוק is ויקרא 22:4.

phrases.english: and this phrase "until he becomes pure"
means until he brings his atonement offering,
why do I need two verses about holy food?
phrases.notes: The second פסוק is the one about a woman after childbirth, ויקרא 12:8.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining the three פסוקים for תרומה, the גמרא now asks a parallel question about קדשים according to another תנא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does the Torah need both the יולדת פסוק and the זב/מצורע פסוק to teach that atonement must come before eating קדשים?

steps.title: Both verses are needed because each case has its own special feature
steps.stepSummary: Each case could be seen as special. A יולדת has a long impurity, and a זב is never permitted at all. So we could not learn one case from the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both are needed. If the Torah had written it only about a יולדת, I would say that is because her impurity lasts so long, but not for a זב. If it had written it only about a זב, I would say that is because he is never permitted at all, but not for a יולדת. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a classic 'צריכא': each פסוק teaches something we could not have learned from the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A יולדת is impure for a long time (40 or 80 days), so maybe only she must wait for her קרבן. A זב stays fully forbidden the whole time, while a יולדת becomes permitted to her husband partway through. Since each case has a feature that might make it stricter, neither can be learned from the other.

keyTerms.meaning: They are needed: each source teaches something the other cannot
A woman after childbirth
Her impurity lasts a long time
Never released from his general prohibition; he is never partly permitted

steps.whatToRemember: A 'צריכא' answer shows that each case has its own reason to be strict, so the Torah must state both.

phrases.english: They are both needed,
for if the Torah had written it only about a woman after childbirth,
I would say it is because her impurity is long,
but for a zav, I would say not.
And if the Torah had written it only about a zav,
I would say it is because he is never released from his prohibition,
phrases.notes: A יולדת becomes permitted to her husband partway through her days, but a זב never gets that break.

phrases.english: but for a woman after childbirth, I would say not,
so both are needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The יולדת has a long impurity and the זב is never permitted at all. Each has a special strictness, so neither case can be learned from the other.

steps.title: Why do we need the verse about the impure vessel?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the Torah needs the פסוק about an impure vessel that 'must be put into water and is impure until evening.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need the פסוק 'It must be put into water, and it is impure until evening'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about yet another פסוק that seems extra. This sets up רבי זירא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already learned that sunset is needed after immersion ('ובא השמש וטהר'). So a פסוק saying an immersed vessel stays impure until evening looks like a repeat. The גמרא wants to know what new thing it teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: It must be put into water, meaning immersed
Until evening, meaning until nightfall

phrases.english: "It must be put into water, and it is impure until evening"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:32. It is about a vessel that touched a dead שרץ.

phrases.english: why do I need it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the קדשים פסוקים to another פסוק about purity that seems to repeat what we know.
steps.triggerLanguage: ״בַּמַּיִם יוּבָא וְטָמֵא עַד הָעֶרֶב״ לְמָה לִי
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new law does the impure-vessel פסוק teach, beyond the sunset requirement we already know?

steps.title: רבי זירא: the verse teaches about touching
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers that the פסוק teaches about touching: until nightfall, the immersed item still makes תרומה impure if it touches it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: it is for touching.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא gives a one-word answer: the פסוק is about touching, not only eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier פסוקים taught that a טמא person may not eat תרומה before sunset. This פסוק adds that before sunset the item even passes impurity to תרומה just by touching it. A vessel does not eat, so 'impure until evening' must be about what it does by touching.

keyTerms.meaning: Touching; passing impurity through contact

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think immersion does nothing before sunset. It helps for some things (see the next step), but for תרומה the item is still impure enough to make it טמא by touching.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
It is for touching.
phrases.notes: Until nightfall it makes תרומה impure just by touching it, not only by eating.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק teaches that before sunset the immersed item passes impurity to תרומה by touching.

steps.title: A ברייתא: pure for מעשר, still impure for תרומה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows the same פסוק says both 'impure' and 'pure.' It explains that after immersion the item is pure for מעשר but impure for תרומה until evening. This supports רבי זירא.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'and it is impure' might mean impure for everything, so the פסוק says 'then it is pure.' 'Then it is pure' might mean pure for everything, so the פסוק says 'and it is impure.' How do these fit together? One is about מעשר and the other is about תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up רבי זירא. The ברייתא resolves a pair of words in the same פסוק that seem to contradict each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls the immersed vessel both 'impure until evening' and 'pure.' The ברייתא answers that it is pure for מעשר right after immersion but still impure for תרומה until nightfall. Since a vessel doesn't eat, being 'impure' for תרומה must mean it makes תרומה impure by touching, which is exactly רבי זירא's point.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא
One might think it applies in every respect
Therefore the פסוק says
How do these fit together?
Here, second tithe, which needs only immersion

steps.whatToRemember: After immersion and before sunset there is an in-between stage: already pure for מעשר, but still impure for תרומה, even by touching.
steps.whyThisMatters: This in-between stage (called טבול יום) shows that purity can come in levels, depending on how holy the food is.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
"And it is impure": one might think it is impure for everything,
so the verse says: "Then it is pure."
If only "then it is pure," one might think it is pure for everything,
so the verse says: "And it is impure."
How do these fit together?
Here it is about tithe, there it is about teruma.
phrases.notes: 'Pure' is for מעשר, right after immersion. 'Impure until evening' is for תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to support רבי זירא's answer in step 10.
steps.raayaObject: רבי זירא's claim that the impure-vessel פסוק teaches the item still makes תרומה impure until evening
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that splits 'וטמא' and 'וטהר' in the same פסוק between תרומה and מעשר

steps.title: Why not reverse it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's split: maybe it should be pure for תרומה and impure for מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But I could flip it around!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why we decided the immersed item is pure for מעשר and impure for תרומה. Maybe it should be the other way around.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא read one פסוק as saying both 'impure' and 'pure.' But the פסוק never says which word goes with תרומה and which goes with מעשר. So the challenge is: what makes us assign them this way and not the reverse?

keyTerms.meaning: I can reverse it. This challenges which way a rule was assigned.

phrases.english: But I can reverse it!
phrases.notes: Reverse it means: say it is pure for תרומה and impure for מעשר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how the ברייתא in step 11 assigned 'impure' and 'pure.'
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's assignment: impure for תרומה, pure for מעשר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק itself does not say which category gets which word, so the opposite assignment seems equally possible.

steps.title: תרומה is stricter, so it gets the stricter rule
steps.stepSummary: Since eating תרומה is stricter than eating מעשר, touching תרומה should also be stricter than touching מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense this way. Eating תרומה is treated more strictly than eating מעשר. So touching תרומה should also be treated more strictly than touching מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that logic decides it. תרומה is already the stricter one for eating, so it should also be the stricter one for touching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know that the rules for eating תרומה are stricter than the rules for eating מעשר. The גמרא extends that same pattern to touching. So the stricter word, 'impure,' goes with תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is logical. It makes sense this way.
Is stricter, treated more seriously.
Eating
Touching

phrases.english: It is logical: just as
the eating of תרומה is stricter than the eating of מעשר,
so too, the touching of תרומה is stricter
than the touching of מעשר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the reversal challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical reasoning (סברא) from an existing pattern of strictness
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Either assignment of 'impure' and 'pure' could fit the פסוק.
steps.terutzMaskana: תרומה is stricter for eating, so it is also stricter for touching. The 'impure' goes with תרומה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule that the leftover impurity until nightfall applies to תרומה and not to מעשר.

steps.title: A second source: 'בכל קדש לא תגע'
steps.stepSummary: Another way to source the rule about touching תרומה: the פסוק 'she shall touch no holy thing,' which a ברייתא first reads as a warning against eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you want, say that the rule about touching תרומה comes from here: 'She shall touch no holy thing.' This is a warning for someone who eats.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a different source for the touching rule. It quotes a ברייתא that reads 'she shall touch no holy thing' as a warning about eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now, the touching rule came from רבי זירא's reading of the vessel פסוק. Now a new פסוק is brought in. Strangely, the ברייתא says this פסוק, which says 'touch,' is really about eating. The next steps explain why, and how touching is still learned from it.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say. This introduces a second, different answer.
It is derived from here.
A warning, the Torah's prohibition behind a punishment
A holy thing. Here it covers holy food like תרומה.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
the touching of תרומה is derived from here:
"She shall touch no holy thing"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 12:4

phrases.english: this is a warning for one who eats.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא נְגִיעָה דִתְרוּמָה מֵהָכָא נָפְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second source for the touching rule, instead of the one built in steps 10 to 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative source from a different פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The touching rule comes only from the vessel פסוק as רבי זירא explained.
steps.terutzMaskana: The touching rule can also come from 'בכל קדש לא תגע.'
steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק says 'touch,' but the ברייתא says it is a warning about eating. That is not a mistake. The next steps explain it.

steps.title: Maybe it really means touching?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks: perhaps the פסוק is just a warning for one who touches, like it plainly says.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe it is only a warning for someone who touches?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises the obvious question. The פסוק says 'touch,' so maybe it is simply about touching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This question tests the claim from step 14 that the פסוק is about eating. The plain words point to touching. The ברייתא now needs a proof that eating is meant.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps it is only. A ברייתא formula for testing another possible reading.

phrases.english: Or is it only for one who touches?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reading given in step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the פסוק warns against eating or simply against touching, as its words suggest.

steps.title: Holy food is compared to the מקדש, so it must mean eating
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק puts 'holy thing' next to 'the מקדש.' Entering the מקדש while impure carries a death-level punishment. So the holy-thing prohibition must also be one with such a punishment, and only eating qualifies, not touching.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'She shall touch no holy thing, nor come into the מקדש.' It compares holy food to the מקדש. Entering the מקדש is something that carries the loss of life. So the holy-food rule must also be about something that carries the loss of life. Touching does not carry the loss of life.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא proves the פסוק means eating. Holy food is linked to the מקדש, and only eating holy food while impure carries a punishment as serious as entering the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a הקש: two things placed together in one פסוק share their rules. Entering the מקדש while impure carries כרת, a death-level punishment. So the 'holy thing' prohibition must also carry a death-level punishment. Eating holy food while impure does (for תרומה, מיתה בידי שמים), but merely touching it carries no such punishment, so the פסוק must mean eating.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches. This introduces the proof.
Compares. It makes a הֶקֵּשׁ, linking two things written side by side.
The Holy Temple
Taking of life, a death-level punishment such as כָּרֵת

phrases.english: The verse states:
"She shall touch no holy thing,
nor come into the Sanctuary."
It compares the holy thing to the Sanctuary:
just as the Sanctuary
is a matter that involves the taking of life,
phrases.notes: Entering the מקדש while impure is punished with כרת.

phrases.english: so too the holy thing
must be a matter that involves the taking of life.
But with touching, there is no taking of life.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר בְּכׇל קֹדֶשׁ לֹא תִגָּע וְאֶל הַמִּקְדָּשׁ לֹא תָבֹא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15 and proves the reading of step 14.
steps.raayaObject: That 'בכל קדש לא תגע' is a warning against eating, not touching
steps.raayaSupportSource: The הקש in the same פסוק between holy food and the מקדש, which carries נטילת נשמה

steps.title: Why say 'touch'? Touching is like eating
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק used the word 'touch' to teach that touching follows the same rule as eating. That is how the touching rule for תרומה comes from this פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the reason the פסוק said it using the word 'touching' is to say this: touching is like eating.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains why the פסוק says 'touch' if it means eating. The word teaches that touching follows the same rule as eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The main warning of the פסוק is about eating. But the Torah chose the word 'touch' on purpose, to put touching under the same rule. So a person who is not yet fully pure may not touch תרומה until nightfall, just as he may not eat it. This finishes the second source for the touching rule.

keyTerms.meaning: That it expressed it in the language of. This explains why a certain word was chosen.
Touching is like eating; both have the same rule.

steps.whatToRemember: There are two sources for the rule about touching תרומה. One is רבי זירא's reading of the vessel פסוק, with logic assigning the strictness to תרומה. The other is 'בכל קדש לא תגע': it is a warning about eating, and its word 'touch' teaches that touching is like eating.

phrases.english: And the fact that it expressed it in the language of touching:
this is what it is saying:
touching is like eating.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַאי דְּאַפְּקֵיהּ בִּלְשׁוֹן נְגִיעָה הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the leftover question from step 16: if the פסוק means eating, why does it say 'touch'?
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining why a word was chosen
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the פסוק is about eating, the word 'touch' seems out of place.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word 'touch' teaches that touching is like eating, which gives us the touching rule for תרומה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It completes the second source for why touching תרומה before nightfall is forbidden.

steps.title: Which תנא lets a woman awaiting a disqualifying union eat תרומה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a פצוע דכא and asks which תנא holds that a woman waiting for a ביאה that would disqualify her by Torah law may still eat תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said about one with crushed testicles, etc. Who is the תנא who holds that a woman waiting for a disqualifying ביאה, a Torah-level one, may eat?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new discussion on the משנה about a פצוע דכא. It asks which תנא agrees with the משנה's ruling, setting up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the wife of a פצוע דכא lives with him, she becomes פסולה to כהונה by Torah law. Even so, the משנה lets her eat תרומה until that happens. The גמרא wants to know which opinion allows eating while she is 'standing ready' for a disqualifying ביאה.

keyTerms.meaning: A man whose reproductive organs were crushed; he may not marry a regular Jewish woman
Who is the תנא? A question asking which opinion a teaching follows
Waiting for, standing ready for
A union that disqualifies the woman from כהונה
By Torah law

phrases.english: One with crushed testicles, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה: his wife may still eat תרומה as long as they haven't been together since the injury.

phrases.english: Who is the tanna
that a woman waiting for a disqualifying intercourse
of Torah law may eat?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic on a new phrase of the משנה, separate from the earlier תרומה-touching discussion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that a woman awaiting a Torah-level disqualifying ביאה may eat תרומה.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: it follows רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר answers that this is a מחלוקת, and the משנה follows רבי אלעזר ורבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: it is taught as a מחלוקת, and this משנה is the view of רבי אלעזר ורבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers the question. He says not everyone agrees with the משנה, and it follows the view of רבי אלעזר ורבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known מחלוקת about a woman who is only betrothed to a כהן she is forbidden to, such as a widow to a כהן גדול. רבי מאיר says she may not eat תרומה. רבי אלעזר ורבי שמעון say she may eat until the forbidden ביאה happens. So, says רבי אלעזר, our משנה follows them and not רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: It is taught as a dispute
The אמורא who gives this first answer (a different person from the תנא of the same name)
The תנא who, together with the תנא רבי אלעזר, lets such a woman eat

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different people named רבי אלעזר here. The one who 'said' this answer is the אמורא. The 'רבי אלעזר' he names, together with רבי שמעון, is an earlier תנא.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
It is taught as a dispute,
and it is the view of Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי אלעזר ורבי שמעון, not רבי מאיר.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: it can follow even רבי מאיר, because she already ate
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the משנה can fit even רבי מאיר, because this woman was already eating תרומה before her husband was injured.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: you can even say it follows רבי מאיר. Here is different, because she already ate.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a different answer. He says the משנה does not have to follow only one side of the מחלוקת. Even רבי מאיר would agree here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's strict ruling is about a woman who never started eating. This wife was already eating תרומה through her husband before his injury, and she has done nothing to lose that right. So even רבי מאיר lets her keep eating.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say
Here it is different
Because she already ate

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole back-and-forth that follows: does 'she already ate' give a woman a lasting right to תרומה?

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
You can even say it is Rabbi Meir,
for here it is different, since she already ate.
phrases.notes: She ate תרומה through her husband before he was injured.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer that disagrees with רבי אלעזר's choice of תנא in step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case (חילוק): this woman already had the right to eat.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה must follow רבי אלעזר ורבי שמעון, because רבי מאיר forbids a woman awaiting a disqualifying ביאה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even רבי מאיר agrees here, because she already ate before the injury.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר rejects 'she already ate' using a widow
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר does not accept the 'already ate' reason. If it were true, a בת ישראל married to a כהן could keep eating after he dies, which is clearly wrong.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר? We do not say 'since she already ate.' Because if you don't say so, then a בת ישראל who married a כהן and her husband died should be allowed to eat, since she already ate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי אלעזר did not use רבי יוחנן's reason. He proves from a widow that having eaten before does not keep the right to eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בת ישראל eats תרומה only because of her כהן husband. Once he dies, she stops, even though she ate during his life. So 'she already ate' cannot be a reason to keep eating. That knocks out רבי יוחנן's way of fitting the משנה with רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not say (this reasoning)
For if you don't say so
A daughter of a regular Jew (not from a כהן family)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar?
phrases.notes: Meaning: why didn't רבי אלעזר answer like רבי יוחנן?

phrases.english: We do not say 'since she already ate.'
For if you don't say so,
an Israelite woman who married a priest
and her husband died should eat,
since she already ate.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, שֶׁכְּבָר אָכְלָה לָא אָמְרִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains רבי אלעזר's rejection of רבי יוחנן's reasoning in step 20.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If eating before kept the right alive, a widow of a כהן would keep eating, and we know she does not.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the 'already ate' reason as a general rule, and with it the claim that the משנה fits רבי מאיר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Having eaten before cannot be a reason, as the widow case shows.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: in the widow's case the marriage ended, but here it did not
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן separates the cases. When the husband dies the marriage is over, but when he is injured the marriage still exists.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן? There, his acquisition ended. Here, his acquisition has not ended.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן defends his answer. He shows that the widow case is not like our case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A widow stops eating because her marriage to the כהן ended with his death, so there is no link left to eat through. The wife of a פצוע דכא is still fully married to him; only living together is forbidden. So 'she already ate' works here, because the connection that let her eat is still in place.

keyTerms.meaning: Ended, lapsed
His acquisition, meaning his marriage bond to her
There / here, used to contrast two cases

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר: the משנה follows רבי אלעזר ורבי שמעון, and 'already ate' is not a reason. רבי יוחנן: it fits even רבי מאיר, because she already ate and her marriage has not ended. A widow is different because her marriage is over.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan?
phrases.notes: Meaning: how does רבי יוחנן answer the widow proof?

phrases.english: There, his acquisition has ended,
phrases.notes: Once the husband dies, the marriage is over.

phrases.english: here, his acquisition has not ended.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אלעזר's widow proof in step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (חילוק) by whether the marriage still exists.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The widow case proves that 'already ate' never gives a lasting right to תרומה.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Already ate' works only while the marriage still exists. A widow's marriage ended, but a פצוע דכא's wife is still married.

steps.title: A ברייתא defines who counts as a פצוע דכא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'איזהו פצוע' and brings a ברייתא: anyone whose testicles were wounded, even just one, or punctured, decayed, or partly missing, is a פצוע דכא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה asks who counts as a פצוע. Our Rabbis taught: Who is a פצוע דכא? Anyone whose testicles were wounded, even only one of them, even if they were only punctured, even if they decayed, and even if part of them is missing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It explains the משנה's question 'who is a פצוע?' by quoting a ברייתא that gives a definition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא makes the category wide. It is not limited to crushing both testicles: an injury to one is enough, and so are a puncture, decay, or a missing part. Each 'ואפילו' adds a milder case that is still included.

keyTerms.meaning: A man whose testicles were injured; he may not marry a regular Jewish woman
'Our Rabbis taught': the opening words of a ברייתא
They were punctured
They decayed or rotted away
They are missing a part

steps.whyThisMatters: This definition decides who is forbidden to marry into the community, so the borders of the category matter in practice. The גמרא will soon test one of its items, the punctured case.

phrases.english: Who is a 'פצוע'?
Our Rabbis taught: Who is a man with crushed testicles?
Anyone whose testicles were wounded,
and even just one of them,
and even if they were punctured,
and even if they decayed,
and even if they are partly missing.

steps.triggerLanguage: איזהו פצוע. תנו רבנן: איזהו פצוע דכא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the תרומה discussion and begins explaining the next phrase of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any wound to the testicles, even to one, and even a puncture, decay, or partial loss, makes a man a פצוע דכא.

steps.title: A man with only one testicle is fit
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה reports from the Sages in the vineyard of יבנה that a man who has only one testicle is just a סריס חמה and is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל, son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, said: I heard from the Sages in the vineyard in יבנה that anyone who has only one testicle is nothing more than a סריס חמה, and he is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: A second teaching is added, about a man who has only one testicle. It rules that he is כשר and may marry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching compares him to a סריס חמה, someone whose condition comes about naturally, and not to a פצוע דכא. The comparison is the reason he is not disqualified. The גמרא will question the exact wording in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A eunuch by nature, whose condition comes from birth and not from an injury
Fit; here, allowed to marry into the community
'The vineyard in יבנה': the Sages' study gathering in יבנה

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka, said:
I heard from the Sages in the vineyard in Yavne:
phrases.notes: The 'vineyard' is the name for the Sages' gathering in יבנה.

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁאֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא בֵּיצָה אַחַת —
phrases.english: Anyone who has only one testicle
is nothing other than a eunuch by nature,
and he is fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה: שמעתי מפי חכמים בכרם ביבנה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a related teaching that marks the edge of the ברייתא's category: a man with one testicle is not disqualified.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man who has only one testicle is like a סריס חמה and is כשר.

steps.title: Is he really a סריס חמה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to the wording: how can this man be called an actual סריס חמה?
steps.simpleTranslation: Can it really enter your mind that he is a סריס חמה?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the exact words of רבי ישמעאל's teaching. Calling this man a real סריס חמה does not fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A real סריס חמה is a specific, known category. This man does not match its definition exactly. So the label 'he is nothing other than a סריס חמה' cannot be meant literally.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Could it enter your mind?': a way of rejecting a reading as impossible

phrases.english: Can it enter your mind that he is a eunuch by nature?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of the teaching in step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'אינו אלא סריס חמה' in רבי ישמעאל's teaching.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The man described does not literally belong to the category of סריס חמה, so the wording cannot be taken at face value.

steps.title: Correcting the wording: he is like a סריס חמה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rewords the teaching: he is not a סריס חמה, he is like one, and he is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: he is like a סריס חמה, and he is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording of the teaching. It reads 'he is like a סריס חמה' instead of 'he is a סריס חמה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wording changes from 'אינו אלא סריס חמה' (he is nothing other than a סריס חמה) to 'הרי הוא כסריס חמה' (he is like a סריס חמה). The man is compared to a סריס חמה for his legal status, but he is not put into that category. The ruling stays the same: he is כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He is like...': a comparison, not the same thing

phrases.english: Rather: he is like a eunuch by nature,
and he is fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אלא: הרי הוא כסריס חמה, וכשר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording objection of step 25 by rereading the phrase.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The teaching seemed to put the man into the category of סריס חמה itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: He is only compared to a סריס חמה, and like him he is כשר.

steps.title: Can a man with punctured testicles really not have children?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the ברייתא's item 'even if they were punctured' and starts telling a story about a man who climbed a palm tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if they were punctured, can he really not have children? But there was a certain man who climbed up a palm tree...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the ברייתא and challenges the case of punctured testicles. It begins a story that will serve as the challenge, and the story continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא counted a puncture as enough to make a man a פצוע דכא, which implies he cannot father children. The גמרא doubts this and brings a real incident to show that a man with a puncture might still have children. Here we only have the setup of the story; the point comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Fathers children
'But surely...': opens a challenge from a known case
A palm tree

phrases.english: And one whose testicles were punctured cannot father children?
phrases.notes: This goes back to the ברייתא's line 'even if they were punctured' in step 23.

phrases.english: But there was a certain man
who climbed up a palm tree

steps.triggerLanguage: וניקב לא מוליד? והא ההוא גברא דסליק לדיקלא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the one-testicle discussion and goes back to challenge an item in the ברייתא of step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that 'ואפילו ניקבו' makes a man a פצוע דכא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A real incident (continued in the next part) seems to show that a man with punctured testicles can still have children, so a puncture should not disqualify him.
